target_audience.secondary: Data visualization practitioners and industry professionals

design_intent: Extend the IEEE VIS 2026 identity through Swiss/International Typographic Style — a modular grid system, bold geometric forms, and high-contrast dark palette that scales from A2 poster to social media to conference badge. The visual language combines minimalist geometric composition with data visualization aesthetics, honoring the conference's academic rigor while projecting innovation.

anchor_lock.reason: The A2 main poster is the largest format and establishes the complete visual system. Every other deliverable adapts this same visual idea.
must_preserve: Bold geometric forms in accent colors

expansion_logic.reason: Brief asks for a promotional visual system. The key visual is the campaign seed.
Brief emphasizes bold typography as core style element.
Multi-format deliverables require explicit color and visual rules.
Brief explicitly names social media kit with multiple platforms.

omitted_expansions.reason: Twitter header already covers wide horizontal format.
Brief asks for one main poster, no series.
Brief focuses on deliverables, not display context.

execution_notes: All PNGs use dark backgrounds (ink #0A0A0F or surface #1A1A24)
Geometric forms must be abstract and original — do not copy hex-pattern-texture
Logos must appear in correct lockup on every deliverable
Space Grotesk for display, Inter for body, JetBrains Mono for data accents only
A2 poster is the consistency anchor
Badge must be legible at 100×70mm physical size
PPT shows both title slide and content slide in one composite
Social formats maintain same visual idea despite different aspect ratios

visual_direction.palette_strategy: Dark-mode-first: ink #0A0A0F background, primary #00D4FF dominant accent, accent-warm #FF4D6A and accent-cool #6366F1 secondary. High contrast with text-primary #FFFFFF.
visual_direction.typography_strategy: Space Grotesk Bold/SemiBold for display and headlines. Inter Regular for body. JetBrains Mono for technical accents. 1.25 modular scale.
visual_direction.motif_strategy: Geometric Data Forms: abstract hexagonal clusters, network nodes, geometric color blocks. Inspired by data visualization but never literal.

copywriting_strategy.headline_principles: Professional-academic register with forward-looking confidence. Precise, not hyperbolic. Cite conference positioning: 'the year's premier forum for advances in theory, methods, and applications of visualization and visual analytics.'
copywriting_strategy.on_image_text_notes: Main poster: 'IEEE VIS 2026' display, 'November 9–13, 2026' subhead, 'Boston, Massachusetts' location, 'The Premier Forum for Visualization' tagline. Social: same core info adapted. Badge: 'IEEE VIS 2026' + name placeholder + dates. PPT title: full info. Content slides: minimal text.

designer_constraints: must respect design_system.json (must-use) — every prompt cites required_tokens hexes
no AI clichés (random gradients, glowing nodes, generic hex/brain motifs)
no SVG output; no per-deliverable HTML pages; only 00-gallery.html is HTML
preserve any research asset with do_not_replace=true through reference-aware editing
prefer image_edit whenever a reference asset is marked allowed_for_edit=true
all text in English only — no Chinese characters
official logos (IEEE, VIS 2026, VGTC) must not be recreated — use official files
open_questions_for_user: Should the design strictly follow the existing IEEE VIS 2026 color palette from the website, or can new accent colors be introduced?
Is there a specific conference theme/tagline for 2026 beyond the general positioning?
Are there mandatory elements for all deliverables (sponsor logos, accessibility requirements)?
